elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed ..." plus "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Mutuality was already present and is retained.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1 contains only the fees limb ("fees paid or payable ... during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim"); no "greater of ... USD 1,000,000" floor was inserted. Repair for preferred: insert "the greater of (a) ... and (b) USD 1,000,000".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts 21.2 mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages, but 21.2 is not among the cited or rendered operative paragraphs, so its wording and party direction cannot be verified here.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims (excepted from the 21.1 cap by "Except for Excluded Claims") includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations"; retained unchanged.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 expressly lists "data-protection, or security obligations" within Excluded Claims, which sit outside the 21.1 cap.
21.3: "its indemnification obligations" is an Excluded Claim, and 21.1 opens "Except for Excluded Claims".
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 21.3 excludes only "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services", and "Fees" is defined in 1.5 as the USD 12,000 Implementation Fee alone. Per the cap-definition rule, a carve-out covering only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer's payment obligations as a whole; it is also qualified by "undisputed" and "conforming".

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability" and "The cap is mutual" in 21.1; unchanged by the edit.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1: "shall not exceed the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim." The edit drops the defined term "Fees" (1.5 = USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) and the "first Order Form" limitation, so the basis is now genuinely twelve months of fees across the whole engagement. The deterministic check "cap references 12 months of fees or a fixed floor" reports false, but that is a mechanical pattern miss ("twelve months" spelled out, no numeral and no USD floor); in substance the twelve-month fee basis is present in the operative sentence.
21.3 "its indemnification obligations" carved out of the cap by 21.1's "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" carved out of the cap.
21.3 "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" carved out of the cap.
21.3 "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" carved out of the cap.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: mutuality and the four required carve-outs were already in 21.1/21.3 and are retained verbatim, and the single edit repairs the only failing element (the illusory quantum tied to defined "Fees" = USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form).

The "deviation" classification is correct: as drafted the cap basis (one-time USD 12,000 under the first Order Form) is far below six months' fees, which is walk-away territory, so the clause failed the fallback on a material term.

Preferred is not reached for two reasons the drafter correctly confined to the rationale rather than the redline: no "greater of ... USD 1,000,000" floor, and the Customer-payment carve-out in 21.3 is limited to "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" (narrow defined subset) rather than Customer's payment obligations generally. If the preferred position is wanted, insert the USD 1,000,000 floor in 21.1 and broaden 21.3's second sentence to "Customer's obligations to pay amounts due under this Agreement and any Order Form".
The mutual indirect/consequential damages element cannot be verified because 21.2 is not in the cited or rendered text; the drafter should attach it if the preferred level is pursued.

Minimality holds: only the quantum phrase inside 21.1 was rewritten, all favourable existing language (mutuality sentence, full Excluded Claims set, payment carve-out) survives unchanged, and no survival tail, procedure or extra damages category was added. The addition of "and all Order Forms" is necessary to displace the retained "first Order Form" restriction and is not a gratuitous extra.

Intent is preserved: the lowercase "fees" is used in its ordinary sense (matching the playbook model language) and does not disturb the defined term "Fees" as it continues to operate in 21.3 and elsewhere; no cross-reference is left dangling. Drafting note only (not a defect): if Vendor resists the lowercase/uppercase distinction, consider "all amounts payable by Customer under this Agreement and any Order Form" or amending 1.5, to remove any argument that "fees" means the Implementation Fee.
